Only per-event moves larger than the cost floor (bigger Upbit impulses) or cheaper execution could convert it.

text: The dip-buy trigger carries real timing information but the maker scale-in ladder built on it is cost-eaten on the 3-coin Coinone universe. At 15m (composite_z reversion 2.0) and 5m (bollinger 96/2.5), every ladder spec beats the ladder-matched random-entry null by a wide margin (G2 percentile 1.0; null median Sharpe_w -2.29 at 15m, -2.90 at 5m). But gross Sharpe_w is at most 0.61 (15m) / 0.88 (5m), and net Sharpe_w at per-asset coinone_conservative is negative for all 16 specs (best -0.13). Maker rungs and maker take-profits do not close the gap: the first tranche, stops and time exits still pay taker cost, and filled rungs are falling-knife inventory. The losses sit in 2022-2023 and in the ETH sleeve. Without a trigger, the same ladder structure (the random null) loses heavily, so 'buy a part on a dip, more on a further dip, sell on small rises' is negative expectancy at these costs; only the dip trigger keeps it near zero.

The cost-eaten claim is refuted if any ladder spec reaches net Sharpe_w > 0 with G2 passing.

text: Tighter ladders are worse. At 5m, rungs every 0.5 ATR fill 67-72 % of the time against 50-58 % at 1.0 ATR, and those specs have net Sharpe_w -1.57..-1.88, 2022 returns -43..-51 % and worst MTM day -9.5..-11.8 %. The 1.0 ATR specs have Sharpe_w -0.66..-1.44 and 2022 returns -26..-41 %. Every 5m ladder would also fail the binding D19 tail check on 2022 (< -20 %), and the 0.5-ATR 4-tranche specs on worst day (> 10 %). Inventory accumulates in trending declines faster than the reversion pays it back, so more and closer rungs mean more falling-knife exposure, not more liquidity premium.
